messages:
maria_support: Hey team — customer (acct 78910) escalated a billing delta. Their invoice shows ~23k embeddings units for last week but dashboard sums to ~15k. They primarily use the embeddings batch endpoint for reranking. Can someone triage?

devin_billing: Thanks Maria. Can you share the raw request payload or a sample? Also which model/version are they calling?

maria_support: Pasted anonymized example from customer (they said they always batch 128 inputs). Request: `POST /v1/embeddings/batch` body:
```json
{"model":"redwood-embed-1","inputs":["long text...", "short", "...", null, "" /* lots of rows, some truncated by client lib */]}
```
They mentioned some rows end up as empty strings/null after client truncation.

ravi_eng: Hmm empty/null inputs could be causing vector dim fallback. We had a metering handler that assumes all returned vectors match model_dim; if a vector is nil we historically recorded a 0-length vector and then converted billing to per-item pairwise fallback. That could inflate counts if we later double-account. Need logs. Can someone attach trace IDs?

maria_support: Customer provided trace id: trace_0a9b2f (from their response headers). Also see invoice period 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-07.

jen_sre: Pulling logs for trace_0a9b2f now. Quick note: we recently shipped a change to batch normalization that pads mismatched vectors with trailing null bytes for GPU bundling, might interact.

olivia_prod: I see the request in ingress logs: batch_size=128, content-length varies per item. Downstream runtime returned success but with 3 items as `null` vectors in the model response (svc-gen returned dims=[]). Metering pipeline then executed a fallback branch that computed per-input token-equivalent usage for those items and ALSO counted the batch-level tokens — looks like double accounting.

devin_billing: Can you paste the meter events snippet? We need to know whether invoice lines came from pairwise_per_item events vs batch_per_token events.

olivia_prod: Snippet (sanitized):
```
{ "meter_event": "batch_tokens", "value": 15000 }
{ "meter_event": "per_input_vector", "count": 128 }
{ "meter_event": "per_input_vector", "count": 3, "fallback": "null_vector" }
```
The extra per_input_vector lines for the 3 nulls were generated after the batch_tokens event. That matches the 23k invoice aggregate.

ravi_eng: Repro hypothesis: client-side truncation -> some inputs become empty/null -> model server returns empty vector placeholder -> metering detects mismatch in dim and flags those items for separate accounting but doesn't suppress the original batch_tokens event. That leads to double-counting for affected batches.

maria_support: Customer says this is intermittent (happened ~40 batches last week). They can reproduce by sending some inputs as `""` or `null` in the middle of a large batch.

devin_billing: Ok. Finance request: please produce a list of invoice line items (or meter_event ids) for acct 78910 in that period where `fallback==null_vector`. Kate, can you hold refunds until engineering confirms scope?

kate_finance: Hold done. We need a window and count. If engineering confirms double-counting we will process pro-rata credits for the impacted weeks.

ravi_eng: I'll create a reproducible test. Quick repro steps for engineers:
1) curl POST /v1/embeddings/batch with 128 inputs where ~5 entries are `""` or `null`.
2) set header `X-Client-Trace: embed-null-test`
3) watch runtime logs and meter pipeline; assert that only one batch_tokens event emitted and no follow-up per_input_vector fallback for already counted items.

ravi_eng: Local quick fix idea: in metering pipeline, add an atomic check: if batch_tokens event emitted for this batch_id, do not emit additional per-input accounting for the same item_ids; instead tag and emit a corrective flag. I'll open a PR.

jen_sre: We should also add an alert rule for >1 meter_event type for same batch_id within 60s. Will create a pager alert as precaution.

olivia_prod: I will run a small replay of last week's traffic targeting trace pattern and generate a list of affected batches and batch_ids. Will attach to this thread when complete.

support-bot: New ticket created: #SUP-1159 (embeddings metering double-count on null inputs).

ravi_eng: PR #4521 opened: metering: suppress per-item fallback after batch_tokens emit. Added unit tests for null vectors and for mixed-dim responses. Requesting review from @jen_sre and @olivia_prod.

deploy-bot: Deploy started for commit d4e8b3 (metering/suppress-null-fallback) to staging at 2026-11-09T18:12:00Z.

jen_sre: Quick run in staging looks good; no double events on our synthetic null-input batches. Scheduling canary to prod at 5% traffic.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded (5%). Monitoring metrics for extra meter_event spikes.

olivia_prod: Replay finished. Found 42 batches in the invoice window that had fallback==null_vector. Total extra charge exposure ~ $7,800 (USD) for acct 78910. List uploaded to internal drive (link suppressed).

kate_finance: Thanks. Please mark the affected periods in the billing system and prepare a credit memo for acct 78910. We'll draft communication once engineering confirms root fix and production deploy.

deploy-bot: Production rollout completed for commit d4e8b3 at 2026-11-10T01:05:12Z. No regressions seen in 30m watch window.

ravi_eng: Patch released. Added integration test and a metric to increment on suppressed_fallback_count. We'll monitor for 48h.

maria_support: Customer update: confirmed they can reproduce and will pause bulk rerank jobs until we confirm refund. Leaving them on hold.

kate_finance: Credit issued for $7,800 and invoice adjusted. Customer notified.

maria_support: Customer replied: thanks for quick turnaround, will resume and report if anything else shows up. :relieved:

jen_sre: Follow-ups: 1) Add client-linter docs warning about sending `null`/empty strings in batches. 2) Add a dashboard card for suppressed_fallback_count. 3) Run a backfill audit for last 90 days to find other accounts impacted.

ravi_eng: Agreed. I opened infra ticket #INF-678 to schedule the backfill job.

maria_support: Closing loop here. Thanks everyone for the fast response.
